- Overestimate early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days; reduce initial peaks.
- Underestimate when true values spike upward after a low; model tends to lag or underreact to sharp upturns.
- Overshoot after a spike in model forecast; cap or smooth out post-peak values to avoid overcorrection.
- Mean-reversion bias: model often holds high values too long; introduce a decay factor or moving average to dampen persistence.
- Forecast tends to be too optimistic in the final 5–10 days; reduce tail-end values slightly to match observed downward drift.
- When history shows a clear upward trend, model often overfits the trend; apply a trend-stopping rule or limit slope increase beyond 2% per day.
